LESSON: STRING MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS AND DRAWING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: CREATING AND EXECUTING Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Le
Topic 1.1: String Musical Instruments and Drawing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on String Musical Instruments and Drawing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are indigenous string musical instruments necessary in music?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya
2. describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument
3. identify pictures drawn using stippling technique
4. draw a picture of a musical instrument using stippling technique

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: STRING MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS AND DRAWING
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
String Musical Instruments and Drawing helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: STRING MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS AND DRAWING
Study String Musical Instruments and Drawing like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “String Musical Instruments and Drawing” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to String Musical Instruments and Drawing in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify pictures drawn using stippling technique

What this means
In this part you learn to identify pictures drawn using stippling technique. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify pictures drawn using stippling technique.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify pictures drawn using stippling technique. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Draw a picture of a musical instrument using stippling technique

What this means
In this part you learn to draw a picture of a musical instrument using stippling technique. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw a picture of a musical instrument using stippling technique.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “String Musical Instruments and Drawing” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw a picture of a musical instrument using stippling technique. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what String Musical Instruments and Drawing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “String Musical Instruments and Drawing” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to String Musical Instruments and Drawing in your own words. (skill: describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: identify pictures drawn using stippling technique)

Example 4: Show how “String Musical Instruments and Drawing” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: draw a picture of a musical instrument using stippling technique)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach String Musical Instruments and Drawing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya.
3. Practise this skill: describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument.
4. Practise this skill: identify pictures drawn using stippling technique.
5. Make one local Kenya example of String Musical Instruments and Drawing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for String Musical Instruments and Drawing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study String Musical Instruments and Drawing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are indigenous string musical instruments necessary in music?
2. How is overlapping achieved in still- life drawing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what String Musical Instruments and Drawing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya.
5. Be able to: describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
